sentences.sentence: Unequal access to technology and skills can create a digital divide, with women and rural populations among those lacking digital tools.
The study describes developing and implementing a Digital Literacy Training Program and comparing adolescent girls' knowledge and skills about digital tools across two implementation phases.
A quasi-experimental design was used with adolescent girls aged 14–19 years in eight blocks of District Gumla, Jharkhand, at baseline (2017), midline (2019) and endline (2020).
Six blocks were purposively selected as intervention and two as comparison.
Samples were 314 and 272, 318 and 260, and 402 vs 220.
Data came from a semi-structured questionnaire in CAPI interviews, compared by chi-square tests and logistic regression (P < 0.05).
Replacements were used for girls who could not be re-interviewed.
At baseline the share of girls scoring above 13 on total digital literacy was significantly higher in the intervention arm (22.9% vs 17.3%, p=0.1).
At midline it was 63.8% vs 47.2% and at endline 90% vs 41.6% (intervention vs comparison, p 0.00).
Knowledge and uptake of government schemes (>6) was 60.2% vs 32.7% at endline (p 0.00).
Computational thinking showed no significant difference at endline (p 0.38).
The authors report a statistically significant increase in digital literacy and all its elements in the intervention arms compared with comparison blocks.
They state they 'cannot attribute this change completely to implementation of this DLTP only', citing rising household possessions and a Google program already operating.
They did not apply advanced statistics, and the collaborative and productive elements were not assessed.
They conclude the programme 'led to improvement' and call for scale-up of tailor-made training.

introduction: However, unequal access to technology and skills can create a digital divide, leaving some individuals at a disadvantage
This concludes that many people, especially women and rural populations, still lack access to basic digital tools and the skills to use them.

This study demonstrates the development and implementation of a Digital Literacy Training Program (DLTP) to measure and compare the knowledge and skills about the digital tools, its importance and practical usage among adolescent girls during three phases of implementation.
methodology: This study was conducted using a quasi-experimental research design among adolescent girls aged 14–19 years, across eight community development blocks of District Gumla in Jharkhand, India over a period of three years from 2017-2020
measure its effect over a period of three years with the comparator arm at the baseline (in 2017), midline (2019) and endline (2020)
The sample coverage for intervention and comparison arm was 314 and 272 at the baseline, 318 and 260 at the midline, and 402 vs 202 in the endline.
six were purposively selected as intervention blocks (Gumla Sadar, Sisai, Kamdara, Basia, Palkot and Chainpur) and rest two were the comparison (non-intervention) blocks
A semi-structured questionnaire was developed in Computer-Assisted Personal Interviews (CAPI) to collect data in- person by interviewing participants at baseline, midline and endline
respondents with similar age and socio-economic profiles from the same or the adjacent village were used as replacements in the midline and endline
Chi‑square test of significance (P < 0.05) was used to compare the independent variables and DL scores among intervention and comparison arm at baseline, midline and endline.
discussion: In our study, we found that there was a statistically significant increase in DL and it’s individual elements from baseline to midline and then to endline in the intervention arms as compared to comparison blocks

Albeit, we cannot attribute this change completely to implementation of this DLTP only as we observed that there was a significant increase in the total household possessions at the midline and endline as compared to baseline, which might have contributed to improved digital literacy.
it was practically very difficult to assess whether the improvement in outcomes was totally attributable to our program or was a combination of multiple projects operational in that area
Due to this reason, we could not apply advanced statistics to quantify the impact of DLTP.
we could evaluate five elements of DL but the collaborative and productive elements could not be assessed
the digital literacy training programme leveraging different elements of DL led to improvement in individual elements and overall scores in the intervention arms as compared to comparison blocks

There is a felt need to scale-up such training programmes; tailor- made for every setting and weaved within cultural contexts to bridge the existing digital divide in low- and middle income countries like India.
